(1) The residential land use with the exception of the distributive commercial use north of the expressway will generally remain the same. Building siting will change, and row housing may eliminate "funneling" areas that now exist.
(2) Internal street patterns will change. For instance, Idlewood Avenue, currently a heavy traffic carrier, will no longer be a through street. Other streets will be changed, closed, and realigned.
(3) The Downtown Expressway will channelize the existing through traffic and greatly increase the number of automobiles passing through the Randolph Project Area.
After consideration of internal street pattern changes, population, and projected traffic levels, the impact on air quality caused chiefly by vehicular traffic is likely to be negative because of the large numbers of automobiles and trucks moving through the Randolph Area on the Downtown Expressway. Within the project area, the expressway will have an undulating profile, four entrance-exit ramps, and a toll plaza located at Lombardy Street. The combination of acceleration and deceleration of "stop-andgo" traffic on the ramps and proposed grades will produce conducive conditions for high concentrations of the major pollutants produced by vehicles for which air quality standards have been set (hydrocarbons, carbon monoxide, and oxides of nitrogen).
Based on formulas published by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency in its pamphlet Compilation of Air Pollutant Emission Factor (February, 1972), the projected Expressway traffic should contribute approximately the following amounts of pollutants to existing air quality conditions:
Carbon monoxide
5176.6 kg/day
Hydrocarbons
766.6 kg/day
Nitrogen Oxide
858.5 kg/day
Particles
35.1 kg/day
Sulfur Oxide
46.8 kg/day
Aldehydes
25.1 kg/day
Organic Acids
11.6 kg/day
